long_biography.plain_text:
Issam Michael Fares began work as a bookkeeper after graduating from Tripoli College, then expanded and managed catering operations across the Gulf. He formed a Saudi infrastructure joint venture with Ballast Nedam in 1972, ultimately acquiring the Dutch contractor and overseeing large civil-engineering projects.

Fares invested construction profits through Houston-based WEDGE Group, bought out its other partners, and sold Ballast Nedam to British Aerospace in 1989. WEDGE developed controlling investments across industry and services before shifting toward income-producing property. Its current portfolio focuses mainly on American office buildings and hotels, with a separate affiliate managing non-US interests. Fares also established education and research initiatives at universities in Lebanon and the United States.
long_biography.html:
Issam Michael Fares began work as a bookkeeper after graduating from Tripoli College, then expanded and managed catering operations across the Gulf. He formed a Saudi infrastructure joint venture with Ballast Nedam in 1972, ultimately acquiring the Dutch contractor and overseeing large civil-engineering projects.

Fares invested construction profits through Houston-based WEDGE Group, bought out its other partners, and sold Ballast Nedam to British Aerospace in 1989. WEDGE developed controlling investments across industry and services before shifting toward income-producing property. Its current portfolio focuses mainly on American office buildings and hotels, with a separate affiliate managing non-US interests. Fares also established education and research initiatives at universities in Lebanon and the United States.

confidence.reason: WEDGE supports the early employment, Gulf management, Ballast Nedam venture and acquisition, construction-profit reinvestment and sale. Its current site supports the portfolio transition, while Tufts, AUB and Balamand corroborate the educational initiatives without implying Fares personally owns the institutions.

The current WEDGE site maintains his official corporate biography and identifies the group as his investment vehicle. Media Ownership Monitor says he continues to head WEDGE, and current organization data identifies him as chairman.

An American University of Beirut institutional biography and a published Issam Fares curriculum vitae independently identify Bayno in Akkar, North Lebanon. Tripoli references appear to conflate his birthplace with his school and regional city.
WEDGE, AUB, L'Orient-Le Jour and the published curriculum vitae consistently give 1937.
